title: Reported outdoor women’s march in Taloqan on International Women’s Day
location: Taloqan City, Takhar Province, Afghanistan (reported attribution; exact site unverified)
scope: One outdoor march shown in a video posted on X; Afghan Witness could not geolocate the clip and says no other people or cars were visible.
organizer: unknown; media reports cited by Afghan Witness attribute it to members of the Independent Coalition of Afghanistan Women’s Protest Movement.
participants_original: Women are visible marching in the video; no headcount reported. Afghan Witness says no other people or cars were visible.
threshold_50_evidence: No headcount or evidence that 50 or more people participated. The absence of other people or cars in the footage does not establish participant count.

reported_date.summary: The report dates the video-posted march to 8 March 2024.

location.summary: Afghan Witness says media reports attributed the march to Taloqan City, Takhar, but it could not geolocate the video.

setting.summary: The report describes an outdoor road march; public access beyond the visible road and participants is not established.

participants.summary: No count is given. The report says no other people or cars were visible in the clip.

demands.summary: Chants oppose the Taliban and call for Manizha Sidiqi’s release; code as political-process opposition and women’s social-restriction rights demands.

organizer.summary: Media reports cited by Afghan Witness attribute the march to members of the Independent Coalition of Afghanistan Women’s Protest Movement; direct organizer role is not independently established.

state_target.summary: The reported slogans target the Taliban regime and demand release of a detained protester.

state_response.summary: The report discusses broader suppression and warnings but does not identify a response to this specific march.

notes: Separate from the private Takhar/Balkh actions. Evidence is a retrospective April report; its embedded video was not opened or independently geolocated. No threshold inference is made.
open_questions: Can the video be independently geolocated to Taloqan?
How many participants were in the march?
Was the march publicly accessible and did it meet the 50-person threshold?
Did authorities respond to this specific action?
